title: The Line
author: Alexandre Dias
excerpt: The queue had been there when he arrived, and it had not, in any way he could measure, moved. Tobias had, on a small holiday in Berlin, come to a small gallery in Mitte and had joined the queue at ten forty-seven in the morning. At eleven-thirty he had noticed that the queue had not moved. At one o'clock he had asked the woman ahead of him. She had smiled in a way he did not, at first, know how to interpret.

chapters.title: Arrival
chapters.body:
The queue had been there when he had arrived, and it had not, in any way he could measure, moved.

His name was Tobias Andersen. He was thirty-four. He was, at the specific small moment of arriving in the queue, a small careful Danish civil servant on a small holiday in Berlin, and had, on a small careful recommendation from a small careful colleague, come to a small careful gallery in Mitte to see a small careful exhibition that had, over the last several months, received the specific small careful attention of the specific small careful people who paid attention to such things.

The queue had been outside the gallery.

It had been long. It had extended, from the small careful entrance of the small careful gallery, along the small careful pavement, around the small careful corner, and had, so far as Tobias could see from his small careful position near the beginning, continued for perhaps another two hundred meters before ending — or, at least, before curving out of his small careful sight around a small further corner.

He had, on arriving, joined the small careful end. He had checked the small careful time on his small careful watch. It had been ten forty-seven in the morning.

He had, in the specific small careful way of a small careful Dane in a small careful queue, waited.

At eleven-thirty he had checked his small careful watch again. He had noticed, at the small careful check, that the small queue had not, in the intervening forty-three minutes, moved. He had not, at eleven-thirty, been closer to the small careful entrance of the small careful gallery than he had been at ten forty-seven. He had, in the small careful position he had been in on arrival, remained.

He had, at the small careful check, looked ahead at the small careful queue. The small careful queue had, so far as he could tell, been in the specific small careful configuration it had been in on his arrival. The small careful people ahead of him had been the same small careful people. They had been standing in the same small careful positions. They had, so far as he could tell, not moved either.

He had thought, at eleven-thirty: *the small careful gallery must not have opened yet.*

He had thought, further: *when it opens, the queue will move.*

At twelve-fifteen he had checked his small careful watch again. The small careful queue had, again, not moved.

At one o'clock he had, in the specific small careful way, tapped the small shoulder of the small careful woman in front of him.

He had said, in his small careful German: *entschuldigung — do you know when the small careful gallery opens?*

The small careful woman had, at the small careful tap, turned. She had been a small careful woman of perhaps fifty. She had had small careful grey hair pinned in a small careful way. She had had a small careful book in her small careful hand — a small careful paperback edition of a small careful novel Tobias had, at some small careful university course, read.

She had said, in the specific small careful voice of a small careful Berliner: *the small careful gallery opened at ten.*

Tobias had said: *at ten.*

She had said: *at ten.*

Tobias had said: *but — but the small careful queue is not moving.*

The small careful woman had looked at him for a small careful moment.

She had said: *no. It is not.*

Tobias had said: *has it moved at all today?*

The small careful woman had, at this, been quiet for a moment.

She had said, quietly: *not since I arrived.*

Tobias had said: *when did you arrive?*

The small careful woman had said: *a small careful while ago.*

Tobias had said, more carefully: *how long a while.*

The small careful woman had, at this, done something Tobias had not, at any point in his small careful life, seen a small careful stranger in a small careful queue do. She had smiled — in the specific small careful way of a small careful woman who had, in the specific small careful way, been in the small careful queue for a length of time she did not entirely want to specify.

She had said, quietly: *long enough.*

Tobias had said: *how — how long is long enough.*

The small careful woman had said, in the same small careful voice: *long enough that I no longer, in the specific small careful way, remember exactly.*

She had, at this, turned back to face forward.

Tobias had, at the small careful position in the small careful queue, been very still.

He had, at last, tapped the small shoulder of the small careful man in front of the small careful woman.

The small careful man had, at the small careful tap, turned. He had been a small careful man of perhaps seventy. He had been wearing a small careful tweed jacket. He had had, on his small careful lapel, a small careful badge from a small careful conference from — Tobias had, in the specific small careful way of a man reading a small careful badge, checked it — from 2014.

Tobias had said: *entschuldigung — how long have you been in the queue.*

The small careful man had, at this, smiled in the same small careful way.

The small careful man had said: *ah. You are a new one.*

Tobias had said: *what does that mean.*

The small careful man had said: *it means, my friend, that you have not, in the specific small careful way, been here long enough yet to stop asking.*

chapters.title: Attempts to Leave
chapters.body:
He had, over the following several hours, learned certain things.

He had learned, first, that no one in the small careful queue was, in any specific small careful way, sure how long they had been in it. The small careful woman ahead of him had, after some small careful pressing, admitted that she had, in the specific small careful way, come to the queue on a small careful holiday from Hamburg approximately three weeks earlier. The small careful man in the tweed jacket had said that he had been in the queue for approximately eleven years. He had said this in the specific small careful way of a man stating a small careful fact that had, in the small careful passage of time, become simply the small careful fact of his life.

Tobias had, at the small careful mention of eleven years, said: *eleven — eleven years.*

The small careful man had said: *approximately, yes.*

Tobias had said: *but — but you go home. At the small careful end of the day. You come back the small careful next morning.*

The small careful man had, at this, looked at Tobias with a small careful patience.

The small careful man had said: *no, my friend. No one goes home.*

Tobias had said: *what?*

The small careful man had said: *the small careful queue does not permit one to leave. One arrives, and one stays. If you attempt to leave — if you attempt, in the specific small careful way, to step out of the small careful queue — the small careful thing you find is that you cannot. Your small careful body will, in the specific small careful way, not permit you. You will, at each small careful attempt, discover that you have taken the small careful step and have, in the specific small careful way, ended up back where you started. You will, over the small careful weeks, learn to stop trying.*

Tobias had, at the small careful position in the small careful queue on a small careful Wednesday afternoon in November in Berlin, looked at the small careful man.

He had said: *and — and you eat. And you sleep. And you —*

The small careful man had said: *no, my friend. One does not eat. One does not sleep. One does not, in the specific small careful way, do any of the small careful things one does. One only stands in the small careful queue.*

Tobias had said: *for eleven years.*

The small careful man had said: *approximately.*

Tobias had said: *and you are — you are not hungry.*

The small careful man had said: *no.*

Tobias had said: *and you are not tired.*

The small careful man had said: *no.*

Tobias had said, more quietly: *and you are not — not bored.*

The small careful man had, at this, been quiet for a small careful moment.

The small careful man had said, quietly: *at first, my friend. At first one is very bored. And then one is very afraid. And then one is very angry. And then one is very sad. And then, in the specific small careful way, one is none of those things. One is simply — in the small careful queue.*

Tobias had said: *and no one — no one goes into the small careful gallery.*

The small careful man had said: *not that I have seen.*

Tobias had said: *never.*

The small careful man had said: *never.*

Tobias had said: *then what — what is the small careful queue for.*

The small careful man had, at this, done something Tobias had not, at any point in the small careful conversation, seen him do. He had, in the specific small careful way, looked past Tobias.

He had said, in a small careful voice: *for the small careful queue, my friend. The small careful queue is for the small careful queue.*

—

Tobias had, over the small careful following days, tried to leave.

He had tried, at first, in the small careful ordinary way — he had, in the specific small careful way, simply stepped out of his small careful position and had begun to walk along the small careful pavement in the direction he had come from. He had walked, at the first attempt, for perhaps three careful steps. He had, at the third careful step, noticed that he was, in the specific small careful way, back in his small careful position in the small careful queue.

He had, at the second attempt, tried to run.

He had, at the third careful step of the running, been back in his small careful position.

He had, at the third attempt, tried to walk very slowly, in the specific small careful way of a man testing whether a small careful thing was, in the specific small careful way, a small careful matter of speed.

He had, at the third careful slow step, been back in his small careful position.

He had, at the fourth attempt, tried to walk sideways.

He had, at the fifth attempt, tried to walk backwards.

He had, at the sixth attempt, tried to sit down on the small careful pavement.

He had, at the seventh, tried simply to close his eyes and to imagine, in the specific small careful way, that he was somewhere else.

Each small careful attempt had ended in the specific small careful way — with him standing, in his small careful position in the small careful queue, in the specific small careful way he had been standing before.

He had, at the specific small careful end of the seventh attempt, stopped trying.

He had, in the specific small careful way of a man who had, over the small careful several days, been slowly understanding a small careful thing, understood.

He had understood that the small careful queue was not, in the specific small careful way, a queue for the small careful gallery. He had understood that the small careful queue was not, in any specific small careful way, going to move. He had understood that the small careful gallery, whatever it was — whatever it contained — was not, in the specific small careful way, the small careful point.

He had understood that the small careful queue was the small careful point.

He had understood that the small careful queue was, in the specific small careful way, a small careful arrangement to which he had, in the specific small careful way of a small careful Danish civil servant on a small careful holiday, been assigned. That he had, at ten forty-seven on the Wednesday morning, arrived at it, and had, in the specific small careful way, joined it, and would, in the specific small careful way, remain in it for the specific small careful duration of whatever the small careful arrangement required.

He had understood, further, that the small careful arrangement was, in the specific small careful way, kind.

The small careful arrangement did not require him to eat. It did not require him to sleep. It did not require him to work, or to worry, or to attend to any of the small careful small careful things his small careful ordinary life had, over the last thirty-four years, required him to attend to. It did not require him to make any small careful decisions. It did not require him to be anywhere else. It only required him to stand.

He had, in the specific small careful way, over the following small careful weeks, come to understand that the small careful queue was, in the specific small careful way of a small careful arrangement made for him, a small careful gift.

He had, at some small careful point in his small careful third year, stopped counting the small careful days.

chapters.title: The Project
chapters.body:
The small careful queue had continued.

It had continued, in the specific small careful way of a small careful arrangement that had, so far as any small careful person in it could tell, no small careful end. New small careful people had, over the small careful years, arrived at the small careful back of it. Tobias had, over the small careful years, watched them join. He had watched their small careful confusion. He had watched their small careful attempts to leave. He had watched their small careful gradual careful acceptance.

He had, on some small careful occasions, when a small careful new person had, in the specific small careful way of a small careful new person, tapped him on the small careful shoulder to ask him how long he had been in the small careful queue, done what the small careful man in the tweed jacket had, on his own small careful first afternoon, done for him.

He had smiled, in the specific small careful way. He had said, quietly: *long enough.*

The small careful new person had, in the specific small careful way, understood.

He had, over the small careful years, learned certain things about the specific small careful people in his small careful section of the small careful queue.

He had learned that the small careful woman from Hamburg had, over the small careful years, been slowly reading the small careful paperback edition of the small careful novel she had had in her small careful hand on his first afternoon. She had, in the specific small careful way of a small careful woman doing a small careful thing very slowly, been reading it at the rate of approximately one small careful sentence per year. She had, in his small careful eleventh year in the small careful queue, been on page nine.

He had learned that the small careful man in the tweed jacket had, over his small careful decades in the queue, been slowly, in the specific small careful way, humming.

He had learned that the small careful man three careful positions ahead of him had, over his own small careful time in the queue, been slowly working out — in the specific small careful way of a small careful mathematician — a small careful proof of a small careful theorem he had, on the small careful outside, not quite been able to finish.

He had learned that everyone in the small careful queue had, in the specific small careful way, a small careful project.

He had understood, in the specific small careful way of a man in his own small careful seventh year in the queue, that this was the small careful arrangement. The small careful queue had, in the specific small careful way, given each small careful person in it the small careful gift of a small careful infinite quantity of small careful time in which to work, without interruption, on the small careful specific thing they had, in their small careful outside lives, not had the small careful time to work on.

Tobias had, in his small careful seventh year, understood that his own small careful project was, in the specific small careful way, going to be a small careful thinking.

He had, over the small careful thirty-four years of his small careful ordinary life, been in the specific small careful way of a man who had, at every small careful moment, been thinking about the small careful next small careful thing. He had, over those small careful years, not, at any point, had the small careful time to think about the small careful current small careful thing. He had, in the small careful queue, been given the small careful time.

He had, over the small careful decades, thought.

He had thought about his small careful childhood in Aarhus. He had thought about his small careful mother, who had died when he had been twenty-one. He had thought about the small careful woman he had, at twenty-seven, briefly loved and had, at twenty-eight, in the specific small careful way of a small careful young Danish man, not married. He had thought about the small careful career he had had at the small careful ministry, and about the small careful careful decisions he had, over the small careful years, made in it, and about the small careful ways in which those small careful decisions had, in the specific small careful way, been the small careful decisions of a small careful man who had, at no small careful point in his life, actually been thinking.

He had thought about the small careful whole of his small careful life.

He had, over the small careful decades in the small careful queue, come to a small careful understanding of it.

He had understood, in the specific small careful way, that his small careful life had been small careful good. That he had, in the specific small careful way, done small careful small careful things, and had been small careful small careful loved by a small careful small careful number of small careful people, and had been, in the specific small careful way, a small careful small careful presence in a small careful small careful world. He had understood that the small careful ordinary shape of his small careful life had been, in the specific small careful way, the small careful shape it had been meant to have.

He had understood, further, that the small careful queue was, in the specific small careful way, the small careful next small careful part of it.

He had, at some small careful point in his small careful thirty-first year in the queue, understood that he was, in the specific small careful way, no longer waiting for anything.

He had, at that small careful understanding, been at peace.

—

The small careful queue had, in the specific small careful way of the small careful queue, gone on.

It has, so far as Tobias knows, still not moved. New small careful people have, over the small careful years since his small careful understanding, continued to arrive. The small careful woman from Hamburg has, by his small careful count, reached page seventeen of her small careful paperback. The small careful man in the tweed jacket has, over the small careful decades, not, in the specific small careful way, changed the small careful tune he has been humming.

The small careful gallery, so far as anyone in the small careful queue has ever been able to determine, has not, in the specific small careful way, ever opened its small careful doors to anyone in the small careful queue. It has, in the small careful way, remained open to the small careful outside world. Small careful people on the small careful outside have, over the small careful decades, come and gone from it, in the specific small careful way of small careful people visiting a small careful gallery. None of them have, at any point, seemed to notice the small careful queue.

Tobias has, in his own small careful position in the small careful queue, over the small careful decades, watched them.

He has watched them come. He has watched them go. He has watched them, in their small careful small careful ordinary lives on the small careful outside, hurrying about their small careful small careful ordinary business. He has, in the specific small careful way, felt for them the specific small careful kind of quiet careful sadness one feels for people who are, in the specific small careful way, still — as he had been, in his own small careful ordinary life — thinking about the small careful next small careful thing.

He has, in the specific small careful way, not envied them.

He has understood, in the specific small careful way of a man who has, in the small careful queue, been given the small careful gift of being permitted to stop, that he is, in the specific small careful way, in the small careful place that certain small careful people are given in return for having been, at some small careful point in their small careful lives, willing to stand still.

He does not, at this small careful moment, know how long he has been in the small careful queue. He has, in the specific small careful way, stopped counting.

He does not, at this small careful moment, know how much longer he will be in it. He does not, in the specific small careful way, mind.

He is, in the specific small careful way of a small careful man in a small careful queue, at peace.

He will, in the specific small careful way, remain until the small careful queue is, in whatever specific small careful way, done with him.

He does not, at this small careful moment, expect that to be soon.
